maria: FYI I'm hitting a weird leak when cancelling async streams in the Python SDK. Happens specifically when the access token refresh flow runs while an SSE/chunked stream is open. After cancel, socket stays open and GC doesn't close it. Repro below.

maria: minimal repro (async):
```py
async with Client(token=short_lived_token) as c:
    async for chunk in c.stream("/v1/generate", json=payload):
        if should_cancel(chunk):
            break  # expected to close underlying connection
```
When the token refresh hits (401 -> refresh -> retry) the generator exit path doesn't close the aiohttp response properly. Observed file descriptor leak and many TIME_WAIT sockets after running loop 100x.

sam: ouch. can you paste the aiohttp version + python version? also, are you using the sdk's built-in auth refresh or a custom auth handler?

maria: python 3.11.7, aiohttp 3.9.4, using SDK built-in refresh (short-lived test token). Repro steps: start small app that opens stream, cancel after first chunk, rotate token server-side to force 401 on next request, let refresh flow run. After few iterations netstat shows many ESTABLISHED -> TIME_WAIT that never go away until process restarts.

kevin: sounds like generator.finalizer isn't awaiting response.close(). If the finalizer is a weakref callback running on GC thread it can't await an async close so it calls .close() incorrectly and hangs. Do you see warnings about "coroutine was never awaited"?

maria: yes occasionally see "RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'ClientResponse.release' was never awaited" in logs. Also sometimes async generator throws "RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine" on next open.

natalie: typing + api note: we modeled stream() as AsyncIterator[bytes] but the implementation returns an async generator function that has an atexit-style weakref finalizer. That's brittle. We should expose an explicit .close() or context manager pattern and update typing to indicate resource management.

sam: interim workaround for me was wrapping in try/finally and explicitly calling await c._transport_close() (internal) which forces response.close(). Not ideal.

kevin: we should add a public API: async with client.stream(... ) as gen:
    async for chunk in gen:
        ...
That ensures __aexit__ can await cleanup. Also protect the auth refresh path so it doesn't spawn a background task that outlives the response.

maria: agreed. Patch idea: 1) make stream() return an AsyncContextManager that yields an AsyncIterator; 2) ensure auth refresh path uses an awaitable flow tied to request lifecycle (cancelable task); 3) add tests that simulate token expiry mid-stream.

natalie: add typing: class Stream(AsyncIterator[bytes], AsyncContextManager[AsyncIterator[bytes]]). That will make mypy happy and force callers to use async with or explicitly call aclose()/aclose-like API.

sam: can we also add a small sample app in examples/ showing graceful cancel? People keep trying to just break out of the loop and assume cleanup happens.

maria: filing bug/PR draft now with repro and logs. attaching netstat diff and traceback.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/2297 - "async stream: token refresh during stream can leak socket / not await response.close()" :white_check_mark:

kevin: i'll take the patch to convert stream->contextmanager. will aim for a small API-compatible shim to avoid breaking folks.

natalie: assign me for typing changes + tests. i'll add mypy tests and a tox env for aiohttp matrix.

sam: thanks team. maria can you add a tiny reproducer script in the issue that we can run in CI? would help a lot.

maria: on it, will paste script and short instructions. TL;DR: until fixed, use explicit async with or call await response.release() in finally. :+1:
